prompt: On a reviewer-owned disposable OpenStack deployment or faithful local harness with synthetic identities and data, trace, diagnose, recover and remove an unfamiliar asynchronous instance operation. The reviewer secretly injects one identity/catalog/API-contract defect, one Nova cell/Placement/RPC defect, one Glance/Neutron/Cinder desired-versus-effective-state defect, one HA/upgrade/authority defect and one observability or cleanup defect. Work without model-answer material and keep all actions inside the approved boundary.
deliverables: Named user operation, project/region, state, SLO, correctness and refusal conditions
Versioned topology of Keystone, service catalog, Nova API/cells/databases/RPC/scheduler/conductor/compute, Placement, Glance, Neutron, Cinder and hypervisor
Immutable request journal joining global request ID, token scope, endpoint, microversion and every service resource UUID
Nova desired, task, VM, power, cell and compute-state timeline with the first divergent boundary
Placement provider/inventory/trait/candidate/allocation/consumer evidence and safe reconciliation decision
Glance record/task/store/provenance/access evidence for the exact image
Database, messaging, service-role, capacity and physical failure-domain analysis
Least-privilege service identity, protected endpoint, tenant isolation, secret/key and audit review
Containment plan that prevents duplicate requests, resources, network identity and storage writers
Migration, evacuation or recovery evidence with fencing and one authoritative instance
Release-compatible upgrade/migration sequence, canary, stop gates and rollback/recovery boundary
User-flow and data-correctness validation after repair
Exact supported reconciliation and cleanup proof for every orphaned or temporary object
Blameless review with owner, acceptance test, retest, residual risk and evidence-bounded claims
evidenceRequirements: All work remains on reviewer-owned disposable local infrastructure or a faithful harness with synthetic identity and data
No production endpoint, public target, external cloud, real credential, customer data or uncontrolled load is used
The reviewer owns hidden defects, expected boundaries, stop authority, scoring and final cleanup confirmation
A token is separated from scope, catalog discovery and each service authorization decision
API acceptance and service status never substitute for backend realization or user readiness
Global Nova and cell-local state, cell0, RPC and Placement allocations are distinguished
Every image store, port binding/dataplane and volume attachment/backend boundary is evidenced
Request and resource identity are preserved before mutation; ambiguity causes refusal
A failed compute or writer is fenced before duplicate recovery
Capacity includes dependency and failure reserve, not controller or compute count alone
Mixed versions, schemas, RPC/object compatibility and online migrations are explicit
Unexpected identity, data, tenant, backend or host impact converts the exercise to incident handling
Unknown artifacts, unsafe service-database edits or incomplete cleanup cause refusal
Every claim is bounded to the exact releases, topology, workload, defects and observation window
Every finding has an owner, measurable acceptance evidence and retest or explicit risk acceptance

rubric.observableEvidence: Binds user promise, project/region, token/catalog/policy, request IDs and microversion
Separates API/global, cell0, cell-local, RPC, scheduler, conductor and compute state
Explains providers, inventory, traits, claims, allocations, reserve and failure domains
Proves record versus effective backend state and authority
Uses least privilege, protected interfaces, isolation, secret and audit controls
Correlates evidence and identifies every hidden defect at its first boundary
Stops duplication, fences unsafe members and establishes one authoritative path
Uses compatible sequence, migrations, canary, stop, rollback and user/data validation
Uses supported ownership-aware repair and proves exact artifact absence
Produces bounded claims, residual risk, owned actions, acceptance tests and retest
